contentBlocks.body: When a production issue appears, the safest answer is systematic: define impact, check recent deploys, inspect telemetry, reproduce with safe data, mitigate, then fix with regression coverage.
Mitigate first, find the root cause second. Rolling back a bad release takes minutes; a hurried fix-forward under pressure can make the incident worse.

Most incidents follow a change, so line up the error-rate timeline with the deploy and config-change timeline. A spike a few minutes after a deploy makes that deploy the prime suspect, and the mitigation is to roll back to the version before it. A spike hours after the last deploy points elsewhere: a dependency, a traffic change, a data migration, or an expiring certificate. If the suspect is the first release of a feature, there is no known-good version to return to, so ship risky features behind a flag you can turn off.

knowledgeItems.prompt: A deployment caused lesson completion to fail for every user. What is the strongest first response?

choices: Wait to see if users stop reporting it
Delete failed rows manually without understanding why
Mitigate impact with rollback or feature flag, then investigate with logs and metrics
payload.answer: Mitigate impact with rollback or feature flag, then investigate with logs and metrics
payload.explanation: Production debugging balances user impact, evidence gathering, and durable fixes.

payload.text: A reliable incident response prioritizes mitigation, evidence, root cause, and ____ coverage.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Errors spike three hours after the last deploy, and nothing else was released. What is the best next step?

choices: Roll back the last deploy immediately; it is always the cause
Look beyond deploys: dependency health, traffic shape, data changes, and expiring certificates or secrets
Restart every server and close the incident
Wait for the next deploy to fix it
payload.answer: Look beyond deploys: dependency health, traffic shape, data changes, and expiring certificates or secrets
payload.explanation: A long gap between a deploy and the spike weakens the deploy hypothesis. Follow the evidence to the other kinds of change.

payload.text: When the faulty change is the first release of a feature, there is nothing to roll back to, so turn it off with a feature ____.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Triage an incident: find the error spike, match it to a deploy, and choose between rollback, disabling a feature, or investigating further.
